Chapter_name: PRELIMINARY
Section _name: Definitions
Description: Defines key terms like bailable offence, cognizable offence, complaint, investigation, police report, etc.

Chapter_name: PRELIMINARY
Section _name: Trial of offences under the Indian Penal Code and other laws
Description: All offences under IPC shall be investigated, inquired into, tried, and otherwise dealt with according to the provisions of CrPC.

Chapter_name: CONSTITUTION OF CRIMINAL COURTS AND OFFICES
Section _name: Classes of Criminal Courts
Description: Besides High Courts and Courts constituted under any law, there shall be Courts of Session, Judicial Magistrates of first class (Metropolitan Magistrates in metro areas), Judicial Magistrates of second class, and Executive Magistrates.

Chapter_name: ARREST OF PERSONS
Section _name: When police may arrest without warrant
Description: Police may arrest without warrant any person who commits a cognizable offence in presence of police, or against whom reasonable complaint/credible information has been made of committing a cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment up to 7 years (subject to conditions), or generally for offences punishable with imprisonment > 7 years.

Chapter_name: ARREST OF PERSONS
Section _name: Notice of appearance before police officer
Description: Where arrest is not required under section 41(1), police shall issue notice directing person to appear. Person complying shall not be arrested unless recorded reasons exist.

Chapter_name: ARREST OF PERSONS
Section _name: Procedure of arrest and duties of officer making arrest
Description: Police officer must bear accurate, visible identification; Allow arrestee to inform a friend/relative; Prepare memo of arrest.

Chapter_name: ARREST OF PERSONS
Section _name: Right of arrested person to meet an advocate of his choice during interrogation
Description: Arrested person has right to meet advocate during interrogation, though not throughout interrogation.

Chapter_name: ARREST OF PERSONS
Section _name: Arrest how made
Description: Police officer shall touch or confine the body of person to be arrested unless there be submission to custody. No woman to be arrested after sunset and before sunrise except in exceptional circumstances with permission of Judicial Magistrate.

Chapter_name: ARREST OF PERSONS
Section _name: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail
Description: Police officer arresting without warrant must inform arrestee of full particulars of offence and grounds of arrest. If bailable offence, must inform of right to be released on bail.

Chapter_name: ARREST OF PERSONS
Section _name: Examination of arrested person by medical practitioner at the request of the arrested person
Description: Arrested person may request medical examination if it will afford evidence disproving commission of offence or establishing commission by another.

Chapter_name: ARREST OF PERSONS
Section _name: Person arrested not to be detained more than twenty-four hours
Description: No police officer shall detain in custody a person arrested without warrant for longer than is reasonable, and not exceeding 24 hours (exclusive of travel time) without Magistrate's special order under section 167.

Chapter_name: PROCESSES TO COMPEL APPEARANCE
Section _name: Proclamation for person absconding
Description: If Court believes person is absconding to avoid warrant, it may publish written proclamation requiring appearance at specified place and time (not less than 30 days).

Chapter_name: ORDER FOR MAINTENANCE OF WIVES, CHILDREN AND PARENTS
Section _name: Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents
Description: Magistrate may order person with sufficient means to pay monthly maintenance to wife, legitimate/illegitimate minor children, or parents unable to maintain themselves.

Chapter_name: MAINTENANCE OF PUBLIC ORDER AND TRANQUILLITY
Section _name: Power to issue order in urgent cases of nuisance or apprehended danger
Description: District Magistrate/SDM/Executive Magistrate may issue written order directing any person to abstain from certain act or take certain order with property, to prevent obstruction, annoyance, injury, danger to human life, or disturbance of public tranquility/riot/affray.

Chapter_name: INFORMATION TO THE POLICE AND THEIR POWERS TO INVESTIGATE
Section _name: Information in cognizable cases
Description: First Information Report (FIR). Information regarding cognizable offence given to officer in charge of police station shall be reduced to writing. Copy given free of cost to informant.

Chapter_name: INFORMATION TO THE POLICE AND THEIR POWERS TO INVESTIGATE
Section _name: Police officer's power to investigate cognizable case
Description: Officer in charge of police station may investigate any cognizable case without order of Magistrate. Magistrate empowered under section 190 may order such an investigation (156(3)).

Chapter_name: INFORMATION TO THE POLICE AND THEIR POWERS TO INVESTIGATE
Section _name: Police officer's power to require attendance of witnesses
Description: Police officer making investigation may require attendance of witnesses within limits of own or adjoining station. Provided no male under 15 or above 65, woman, or mentally/physically disabled person shall be required to attend at any place other than their residence.

Chapter_name: INFORMATION TO THE POLICE AND THEIR POWERS TO INVESTIGATE
Section _name: Examination of witnesses by police
Description: Police officer may examine orally any person supposed to be acquainted with facts and circumstances of case. Person bound to answer truly generally, except questions exposing to criminal charge.

Chapter_name: INFORMATION TO THE POLICE AND THEIR POWERS TO INVESTIGATE
Section _name: Recording of confessions and statements
Description: Magistrate may record any confession or statement made to him in course of investigation. Confession must be voluntary.

Chapter_name: INFORMATION TO THE POLICE AND THEIR POWERS TO INVESTIGATE
Section _name: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in twenty-four hours
Description: Magistrate may authorize detention of accused in custody (police or judicial) for term not exceeding 15 days. Total detention pending investigation not to exceed 90 days (death/life/10+ years offences) or 60 days (other offences). On expiry, accused entitled to 'default bail'.

Chapter_name: INFORMATION TO THE POLICE AND THEIR POWERS TO INVESTIGATE
Section _name: Report of police officer on completion of investigation
Description: Final Report / Charge Sheet. Police officer shall forward report to Magistrate empowering to take cognizance.

Chapter_name: INFORMATION TO THE POLICE AND THEIR POWERS TO INVESTIGATE
Section _name: Police to enquire and report on suicide, etc.
Description: Inquest report. Police to investigate unnatural deaths (suicide, homicide, accident, suspicious circumstances) and report to Executive Magistrate.

Chapter_name: CONDITIONS REQUISITE FOR INITIATION OF PROCEEDINGS
Section _name: Cognizance of offences by Magistrates
Description: Magistrate of first class (and empowered second class) may take cognizance of offence upon: (a) receiving complaint, (b) police report, (c) information from person other than police officer or own knowledge.

Chapter_name: CONDITIONS REQUISITE FOR INITIATION OF PROCEEDINGS
Section _name: Prosecution of Judges and public servants
Description: No Court shall take cognizance of offence alleged to have been committed by Judge/Magistrate/Public Servant (removable only by Govt sanction) while acting in discharge of official duty, except with previous sanction of Government.

Chapter_name: COMPLAINTS TO MAGISTRATES
Section _name: Examination of complainant
Description: Magistrate taking cognizance of offence on complaint shall examine upon oath the complainant and witnesses present.

Chapter_name: COMMENCEMENT OF PROCEEDINGS BEFORE MAGISTRATES
Section _name: Issue of process
Description: If Magistrate opinion there is sufficient ground for proceeding, issue summons (summons-case) or warrant/summons (warrant-case) for attendance of accused.

Chapter_name: TRIAL BEFORE A COURT OF SESSION
Section _name: Discharge
Description: If upon consideration of record and documents and hearing submissions, Judge considers that there is not sufficient ground for proceeding against accused, he shall discharge accused and record reasons.

Chapter_name: TRIAL BEFORE A COURT OF SESSION
Section _name: Framing of charge
Description: If Judge considers there is ground for presuming accused has committed offence, he shall frame charge in writing.

Chapter_name: GENERAL PROVISIONS AS TO INQUIRIES AND TRIALS
Section _name: Person once convicted or acquitted not to be tried for same offence
Description: Person tried by Court of competent jurisdiction for offence and convicted/acquitted shall not be liable to be tried again for same offence (Double Jeopardy protection).

Chapter_name: GENERAL PROVISIONS AS TO INQUIRIES AND TRIALS
Section _name: Legal aid to accused at State expense in certain cases
Description: Where accused is not represented by pleader and has not sufficient means, Court shall assign pleader for defence at expense of State (Sessions trials and others via notification).

Chapter_name: GENERAL PROVISIONS AS TO INQUIRIES AND TRIALS
Section _name: Power to summon material witness, or examine person present
Description: Court may at any stage summon any person as witness or recall/re-examine any person if evidence appears essential to just decision of case.

Chapter_name: GENERAL PROVISIONS AS TO INQUIRIES AND TRIALS
Section _name: Power to examine the accused
Description: Court may (and generally must) question accused to enable him to explain any circumstances appearing in evidence against him. No oath administered.

Chapter_name: GENERAL PROVISIONS AS TO INQUIRIES AND TRIALS
Section _name: Compounding of offences
Description: Table specifies offences which can be compounded (settled) by specified persons (usually victim), either with or without permission of Court.

Chapter_name: THE JUDGMENT
Section _name: Order to pay compensation
Description: Court imposing sentence of fine or imprisonment may order whole or part of fine to be applied in defraying expenses of prosecution or compensation for loss/injury to victim.

Chapter_name: APPEALS
Section _name: Appeals from convictions
Description: Any person convicted on a trial held by High Court (extraordinary jurisdiction), Sessions Judge, or Metropolitan/Assistant Sessions/Magistrate may appeal to higher court (SC, HC, or Sessions Court) as specified.

Chapter_name: APPEALS
Section _name: Suspension of sentence pending the appeal; release of appellant on bail
Description: Appellate Court may suspend execution of sentence and facilitate release on bail during pendency of appeal.

Chapter_name: REFERENCE AND REVISION
Section _name: Calling for records to exercise powers of revision
Description: High Court or Sessions Judge may call for and examine record of any proceeding before any inferior Criminal Court to satisfy itself as to correctness, legality or propriety of any finding/sentence/order.

Chapter_name: PROVISIONS AS TO BAIL AND BONDS
Section _name: In what cases bail to be taken
Description: Person accused of bailable offence shall be released on bail as a matter of right. Indigent person may be released on personal bond.

Chapter_name: PROVISIONS AS TO BAIL AND BONDS
Section _name: Maximum period for which an undertrial prisoner can be detained
Description: Where person has undergone detention for period extending up to one-half of maximum period of imprisonment specified for that offence, he shall be released on personal bond. (Excludes death penalty offences).

Chapter_name: PROVISIONS AS TO BAIL AND BONDS
Section _name: When bail may be taken in case of non-bailable offence
Description: Magistrate may grant bail in non-bailable offences. RESTRICTIONS: 1. Reasonable grounds to believe guilty of offence punishable with death/life imprisonment. 2. Cognizable offence + previously convicted of death/life/7+ years offence or 2+ cognizable non-bailable offences. EXCEPTIONS: Under 16, woman, sick, infirm.

Chapter_name: PROVISIONS AS TO BAIL AND BONDS
Section _name: Bail to require accused to appear before next appellate Court
Description: Before conclusion of trial/appeal, Court trying case shall require accused to execute bail bonds to appear before higher Court as and when notice issued (valid 6 months).

Chapter_name: PROVISIONS AS TO BAIL AND BONDS
Section _name: Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest
Description: (Anticipatory Bail). High Court or Sessions Court may direct that person be released on bail in event of arrest on accusation of non-bailable offence. Factors: gravity of accusation, antecedents, flight risk, humiliation intent.

Chapter_name: PROVISIONS AS TO BAIL AND BONDS
Section _name: Special powers of High Court or Court of Session regarding bail
Description: HC or Sessions Court may direct release on bail of any person in custody (broader powers than Magistrate). Can set aside/modify conditions imposed by Magistrate.

Chapter_name: LIMITATION FOR TAKING COGNIZANCE OF CERTAIN OFFENCES
Section _name: Bar to taking cognizance after lapse of the period of limitation
Description: Cognizance cannot be taken after: 6 months (fine only offence), 1 year (imprisonment <= 1 year), 3 years (imprisonment 1-3 years). E

Chapter_name: MISCELLANEOUS
Section _name: Saving of inherent powers of High Court
Description: Nothing in this Code shall limit or affect inherent powers of High Court to make such orders as necessary to give effect to any order under Code, prevent abuse of process of Court, or secure ends of justice. (Quashing FIRs etc.)
